newsitem.title: USA: OrthoLogic says FDA approves PMA supplement.
newsitem.headline: OrthoLogic says FDA approves PMA supplement.

text.p: OrthoLogic Corp on Monday said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a supplement to the company's pre-market application covering patients using the OrthoLogic 1000 system to heal non-union bone fractures.
A non-union fracture is a fracture that remains unhealed for a minimum of nine months, OrthoLogic said.

In March 1994, the FDA approved the OrthoLogic 1000 and since that time, the company has maintained a registry of all patients using it. The supplement filing included data from 400 patients with non-union fractures.
Overall, 72.3 percent of the patients on which OrthoLogic received data had their non-union fractures healed. Moreover, the patients healed in an average of 4.9 months.

"We are confident that this data will confirm the OrthoLogic 1000 as the standard for bone growth stimulators and result in our achieving market leadership," said George Oram, chief operating officer.
